ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \triangle ABC$ is an inscribed triangle of $ \odot O$ with $ \angle C=30^\circ$ and the radius of $ \odot O$ is $ 2\,cm$. If point P is a point on $ \odot O$ and $ PB=AB$, what is the length of $ PA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $OA$ and $OP$, extend $OB$ to intersect $AP$ at $H$,\\
by the Inscribed Angle Theorem, $\angle AOB=2\angle C=60^\circ$,\\
since $PB=AB$,\\
thus $\angle POB=\angle AOB=60^\circ$, and $OB\perp AP$, hence $\angle OAP=30^\circ$, therefore $OH=\frac{1}{2}AO=1$,\\
then $AH=PH=\sqrt{AO^2-AH^2}=\sqrt{3}\ (\text{cm})$,\\
thus $PA=2AH=2\sqrt{3}\ (\text{cm})$,\\
therefore, the answer is: $PA=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}\ (\text{cm})$.
